instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Stir with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 2 tablespoons of olive oil, mixing until fully incorporated. The dough will be very wet.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size. This slow rise develops flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pan and Stretch the Dough
instructions.text: Generously grease a 9x13 inch baking pan with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Gently pour the risen dough into the prepared pan. Using oiled hands, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan. It will be sticky. If it resists, let it rest for 10 minutes and try again.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Dimpling
instructions.text: Cover the pan again and let the dough rise for another 30-45 minutes. Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Once risen, use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the focaccia. Drizzle generously with more olive oil, sprinkle with chopped rosemary, and flaky sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through. The internal temperature should be around 90C (195F).

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the focaccia from the oven and carefully transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a final touch of fresh olive oil before slicing and serving warm. Buon appetito!

tips: For an extra airy texture, use a high-hydration dough (more water relative to flour). This recipe uses a good ratio for a classic Genovese focaccia.
Always use good quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the final drizzle. It makes a significant difference in flavor.
Focaccia is best enjoyed warm on the day it's baked. Store leftovers loosely covered at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze slices for longer storage.
article:
Unlock the secrets to a truly unforgettable Italian baking experience with the iconic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. This isn't just any bread; it's a culinary journey to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast, where simplicity and high-quality ingredients transform into something extraordinary. Imagine a golden-crusted, impossibly soft, and fragrant flatbread, its surface dotted with aromatic rosemary and glistening with the finest olive oil. This article will guide you through crafting this masterpiece, ensuring every bite transports you to a bustling Italian piazza. If you're looking for an authentic Focaccia Genovese recipe, you've come to the right place.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?
Focaccia Genovese, or Fûgassa as it's known in the local Ligurian dialect, is the quintessential flatbread from Genoa, Italy. Unlike its thicker, often more bread-like counterparts from other regions, Genovese focaccia is distinctly thin, incredibly tender, and boasts a unique texture characterized by its signature dimples. These indentations are not just for show; they act as tiny reservoirs for a generous amount of olive oil and a sprinkling of coarse sea salt, creating pockets of intense flavor and a wonderfully crisp-chewy contrast.

The "Rosemary Olive Oil" designation highlights two of its most crucial components. High-quality extra virgin olive oil is not merely an ingredient; it's the soul of this focaccia, contributing to its rich flavor, tender crumb, and golden crust. Rosemary, often freshly chopped, infuses the bread with its earthy, piney aroma, perfectly complementing the fruity notes of the olive oil. The magic lies in the simplicity: flour, water, yeast, salt, olive oil, and rosemary – transformed by time and technique into a sublime culinary delight.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil begins with selecting the right ingredients. Quality truly makes a difference here.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (Type 0 or 00):** Approximately 500g. A high-protein flour is essential for developing good gluten structure, which gives the focaccia its characteristic chewiness. If you can't find Italian 0 or 00, a good quality unbleached all-purpose flour or bread flour will work.
*   **Warm Water:** 350-400ml (about 1.5-1.75 cups). The exact amount can vary based on your flour's absorption. It should be lukewarm, around 100-110°F (38-43°C), to activate the yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7g (2 teaspoons). Ensure your yeast is fresh for proper rising.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10g (2 teaspoons) for the dough, plus extra for sprinkling on top.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** 80-100ml (about 1/3-1/2 cup), plus more for greasing the pan and drizzling. This is where you shouldn't skimp on quality. A good, fruity EVOO will elevate the flavor immensely.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs, finely chopped. Dried rosemary can be used in a pinch, but fresh provides superior aroma and flavor.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt:** For sprinkling on top before baking. This adds a delightful textural crunch and burst of salinity.

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Follow this Focaccia Genovese recipe carefully, and you'll be rewarded with a truly authentic Italian treat.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. It will be quite wet and sticky – don't worry, this is normal for a high-hydration dough.
3.  **Knead (or Fold):** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 10-15 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. Alternatively, for a no-knead approach, perform a series of "stretch and folds" in the bowl every 30 minutes for 2 hours (total 4-5 folds).
4.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Lightly grease your mixing bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turn it once to coat, and cover with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan with olive oil. Don't be shy; this oil contributes to the crispy bottom crust.
6.  **Transfer and Dimple:** Gently turn the risen dough out into the prepared pan. Pour about 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil over the dough. With oiled fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan, creating those characteristic dimples all over the surface. Be gentle to avoid deflating too much of the air. Sprinkle with chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.
7.  **Second Rise (Proofing):** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let it rise again for another 30-45 minutes, or until puffy. While it's proofing, preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
8.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown and cooked through. If you like an extra crispy bottom, you can bake it directly on a preheated pizza stone or baking steel.
9.  **Finish:** Immediately after removing it from the oven, drizzle generously with more extra virgin olive oil. This adds moisture, flavor, and that beautiful sheen. Let it cool slightly in the pan before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. Mastering this Focaccia Genovese recipe at home is incredibly rewarding.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
These tips will elevate your Focaccia Genovese recipe from good to absolutely outstanding.

*   **Hydration is Key:** Don't be afraid of a sticky dough. The high water content is what contributes to the focaccia's incredibly tender crumb. Resist the urge to add too much extra flour during kneading.
*   **Good Quality Olive Oil:** We cannot stress this enough. The olive oil is a fundamental flavor component. Invest in a good extra virgin olive oil for both the dough and the final drizzle.
*   **Longer Fermentation for Flavor:** If you have time, consider a cold fermentation. After the first rise, you can place the dough in the refrigerator overnight (8-12 hours). This develops deeper flavors and a more complex texture. Bring it back to room temperature before shaping.
*   **Generous Dimpling:** Really press your fingers into the dough to create those deep dimples. They are essential for holding the olive oil and salt, creating bursts of flavor and texture.
*   **Don't Overbake:** Focaccia should be golden brown, not dark brown. Overbaking can dry it out.
*   **The Final Drizzle:** That last generous pour of olive oil straight out of the oven is non-negotiable. It adds incredible moisture, gloss, and flavor.
*   **Use a Metal Pan:** Metal pans conduct heat more efficiently than glass, leading to a crispier bottom crust, which is highly desirable for focaccia.

## Serving Suggestions
Once you've perfected this Focaccia Genovese recipe, the possibilities for enjoyment are endless.

*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve warm with a side of good quality balsamic vinegar and extra virgin olive oil for dipping.
*   **With Meals:** It's a perfect accompaniment to soups, stews, salads, or any Italian main course.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill it with cured meats (prosciutto, salami), cheeses (mozzarella, provolone), roasted vegetables, or fresh tomatoes and basil.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** Enjoy a slice plain, or perhaps with a smear of ricotta cheese and a drizzle of honey.
*   **Bruschetta Base:** Cut into smaller pieces, toast lightly, and top with classic bruschetta toppings like chopped tomatoes, garlic, and basil.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with variations.

*   **Other Herbs:** Instead of rosemary, try fresh oregano, thyme, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Toppings:** Before the second rise, you can add thin slices of onion, cherry tomatoes (halved), black olives, or even a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese. Just be mindful not to overload it.
*   **Garlic:** Infuse some of the olive oil with crushed garlic before drizzling, or sprinkle finely minced garlic over the dough before baking.
*   **Whole Wheat Flour:** You can substitute up to 25% of the white flour with whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor and added fiber, though it will result in a slightly denser texture.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While more challenging, a good quality gluten-free bread flour blend can be used, though the hydration and texture will require adjustments.

Baking Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a truly rewarding experience, transforming simple ingredients into a masterpiece of texture and flavor. This easy-to-follow Focaccia Genovese recipe ensures you can bring a piece of Ligurian tradition into your own kitchen. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in every tender, olive oil-infused bite!
